developments.text: The proposal comes before the truce expires on 10 January 2027; Beijing's response so far is rhetorical, not retaliation.
developments.title: US 20% tariff proposal on China

developments.text: The November AI rout took the Hang Seng to multi-month lows; it was trading near 22,200 by Thursday.
developments.title: AI sell-off hits Hong Kong tech

for_malaysia: Trade channel: China is Malaysia's largest trading partner, and higher US tariffs on China raise the risk that Chinese exports get diverted into ASEAN, adding pressure on Malaysian steel and manufacturers. For now Beijing is choosing talks over retaliation, which keeps the ringgit and Bursa exporters out of the worst case.

headline: Mainland stocks barely moved and Beijing pushed back verbally on new US tariffs while signalling the trade truce should hold.
numbers_note: The CSI 300 moved only marginally (Wednesday's close was 3,898.24), well inside the filter; Hang Seng's daily change could not be confirmed.

points.text: The US proposed an additional tariff of up to 20% on Chinese goods, which Caixin said could take combined duties to about 45% on some imports, ahead of the trade truce's January deadline.

China's foreign ministry called 'overcapacity' a false proposition and the commerce ministry urged dialogue, but analysts told SCMP that trade talks remain on track; the truce expires on 10 January 2027.
The CSI 300 edged up marginally to close at 3,900.55 on Thursday. No catalyst was reported for the move.
